summary.text: Tom Sell is the Republican nominee for the open West Texas seat in the 19th District, held by retiring Rep. Jodey Arrington. A Lubbock resident who describes himself as a fifth-generation West Texan, he worked for former U.S. Rep. Larry Combest, served as deputy staff director of the House Agriculture Committee, and has run the Lubbock firm Combest, Sell & Associates for about 21 years. He won the Republican primary runoff on May 26, 2026, with 64.3% of the vote.

paragraphs.text: According to his campaign website, Sell is a fifth-generation West Texan; his family moved to Lubbock as sharecroppers in 1906, according to The Texas Tribune.
USA Rice Daily reports he was born and raised in the 19th District, where he met his wife, Kyla.
He earned a bachelor's degree and a J.D. from Texas Tech University; his campaign website says the bachelor's was in agribusiness.

Sell worked in the office of former U.S. Rep. Larry Combest (R-Texas) and served as deputy staff director for the House Committee on Agriculture, which Combest chaired, from 1999 to early 2003, according to The Texas Tribune.
According to his campaign website, he helped advance the Crop Insurance Reform Act of 2000 and the 2002 Farm Bill while working for Combest.
After leaving Capitol Hill he returned to Lubbock and founded the firm now called Combest, Sell & Associates with Combest, and he has run it for about 21 years, according to USA Rice Daily.
In the Republican primary, opponent Jason Corley called him a "career lobbyist."
Sell ran in the 2026 Republican primary for the open 19th District seat, led the seven-candidate March 3 field with 40.4%, and defeated Abraham Enriquez in the May 26 runoff, 64.3% to 35.7%.

He lives in Lubbock with his wife, Kyla; the couple raised four children, and their campaign site says they are active in their church and community and mentor students at Texas Tech's Davis College of Agriculture.
The Tribune reports he has coached Little League.
